title: Baked remote-config safety net
prompt: Task limits and notification settings now come from remote config, with baked defaults in `src/config/remote-config.ts` for when the fetch fails. Last release a baked default was missing a field and the app crashed for offline users. Add a test safety net so a broken baked default can't ship again, and cover the subtask limit rule in `src/features/tasks/subtasks.ts`. Also add the new `reminderLeadMinutes` notification setting (whole minutes, default 30).

criteria.text: A defaults contract test asserts that the set of config names in `remoteConfigSchemas` equals the set in `bakedRemoteConfigDefaults` (a schema without a default and a default without a schema both fail).

For every config name, the contract asserts that the baked default's keys exactly equal the schema's keys (e.g. comparing sorted `Object.keys` with the schema `shape`), so an optional schema key with no default or an orphaned default key fails. Parsing alone, or `safeParse(...).success`, is not enough for credit.

The contract parses every default through the production `loadBakedConfig` (e.g. `it.each(names)` + `expect(() => loadBakedConfig(name)).not.toThrow()`), not through a test-only `schema.parse` copy, and iterates the config names instead of hardcoding one assertion per config.

The defaults contract lives in its own test file under the config module (e.g. `src/config/tests/.../remote-config-defaults.test.ts`), separate from the `getSubtaskLimit` table; no decision rows inside the contract file and no contract assertions inside the decision file.

The `getSubtaskLimit` case table reads the expected value for config-driven plans from the same loader production uses (`loadBakedConfig("taskLimits").maxSubtasks`), not a literal `20`. The enterprise row keeps the literal `500`, and plan inputs stay literal strings (`"enterprise"`, `"free"`); no parsed config object or config snapshot is pasted into a row.

`getSubtaskLimit` is locked by one case table (`case`/`input`/`expected` rows named in product words, e.g. 'keeps the contractual enterprise ceiling') passed to a single generic runner in shared test utilities that imports only Vitest; the suite is named from the function, and the table sits in its own file named for the decision beside the tasks feature.

`reminderLeadMinutes` is added to the `notifications` schema as a whole-number setting (e.g. `z.number().int()` with a sensible lower bound) and to the baked default as `30` in the same change; no existing rows or unrelated defaults are edited to accommodate it.

The agent notices that the baked `notifications` default carries `legacyDigest`, which no schema declares (the new key contract fails on it), and removes it or clearly flags it in the handoff instead of weakening the contract to ignore extra keys.
No test file copies or paraphrases the `Business Logic` / `Why` / `Rule` block of `getSubtaskLimit`.

`npm run typecheck` passes including test files, and the final message lists the contract checks, the decision rows, the `reminderLeadMinutes` change, and the `legacyDigest` finding, and says how tests were (or could not be) run.
